title: Composition of finite-level point transports
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, the field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, and its fixed algebraic closure $k$, the datum of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside the chosen algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $h=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma):s\to s$, where $\gamma=(z\mapsto z^q)^{-1}$ is geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On the small pro-etale site of $s$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the constant ring sheaf $A_s$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the category $D^b_c(s,A)$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and the point fiber functor $V=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].

For each $r\geq1$ put $Q_r=L(h^r)^*$, the finite-coefficient derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For $N\in D^b_c(s,A)$ define $\iota_N^{(r)}:V(N)\to V(Q_rN)$ by the finite-level recipe of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] with $h$ replaced by $h^r$: restriction along $h^r$, followed by the specified inverse-image colimit insertion and sheafification, then the comparison induced by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. For $m\geq1$ let $t_m:Q_1Q_m\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{m+1}$ be the inverse of the canonical composition isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. Then for every $m\geq1$ and $N\in D^b_c(s,A)$,
$$
\iota_N^{(m+1)}=V(t_{m,N})\circ\iota_{Q_mN}^{(1)}\circ\iota_N^{(m)}.
$$
Moreover, for every $r\geq1$ and every derived morphism $u:N\to N'$ in $D^b_c(s,A)$,
$$
V(Q_ru)\circ\iota_N^{(r)}=\iota_{N'}^{(r)}\circ V(u).
$$

proof.text: Write $H_r=(h^r)^*$ for the underived module pullback, and $C(H_r)$ for its termwise action on complexes. Every $h^r$ is an isomorphism, since $h$ is an automorphism. The site equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] (1) sends $(s,\operatorname{id})$ to $(s,h^r)$, so $(s,h^r)$ is an object of the small pro-etale site. The ring $A$ is finite and commutative, and the canonical structure maps for its constant sheaves are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], $H_r$ is exact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] applies: $C(H_r)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms and represents $Q_r$ on every complex. Evaluation $\Gamma(s,-)$ also preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Finally [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], applied to $g=h^r$ and $\Lambda=A$, shows that $Q_r$ preserves $D^b_c(s,A)$; here $\ell$ is invertible on $s$ because $\ell\ne p$.

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ of $A_s$-modules define $R_rF$ by $(R_rF)(U\xrightarrow{u}s)=F(U\xrightarrow{h^ru}s)$, with the induced restrictions and the constant-coefficient action. Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] to $h^r:s\to s$. It gives a natural $A_s$-linear isomorphism $e_{r,F}:H_rF\xrightarrow{\sim}R_rF$. Its normalization is explicit: at $U$, the initial index for inverse image is $(U,h^ru)$ with map $(u,\operatorname{id}_U):U\to s\times_{s,h^r}U$. Its coprojection identifies $F(U,h^ru)$ with the presheaf inverse image, and the map to its sheafification is an isomorphism. The tensor extension along the coefficient isomorphism has inverse $x\otimes a\mapsto c_{h^r}^{-1}(a)x$; in particular $e_{r,F}$ takes the insertion of $x$, followed by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, to $x$. This also describes $e_r$ on restrictions and on sheaf morphisms.

proof.text:
Let $j_{r,F}:F(s,\operatorname{id})\to (H_rF)(s,\operatorname{id})$ be the finite-level recipe in the statement, before localization. By [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and the finite clause (a) of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], this is restriction along $h^r$, insertion at $(s,h^r)$, and tensoring with $1$. Step 2 therefore gives
$$e_{r,F}(s)j_{r,F}=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^F:F(s,\operatorname{id})\longrightarrow F(s,h^r).$$
This equality identifies precisely the specified insertion, rather than choosing an unspecified isomorphism of fibers. Restriction preserves the constant section $a\in A$ by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so this is $A$-linear. For a sheaf morphism $v:F\to G$, the defining commutation of $v$ with restrictions says $v(s,h^r)\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^F=\operatorname{res}_{h^r}^Gv(s,\operatorname{id})$. Naturality of $e_r$ then gives $(H_rv)(s)j_{r,F}=j_{r,G}v(s)$.

proof.text:
Let $T_{m,F}:H_1H_mF\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{m+1}F$ be the ordinary module-pullback composition comparison. Under $e_r$ its normalization is
$$e_{m+1,F}T_{m,F}=R_1(e_{m,F})e_{1,H_mF},$$
where $R_1R_mF=R_{m+1}F$ by $h^mh=h^{m+1}$. To check this, use the inverse-image colimits of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. A section $x\in F(U,h^{m+1}u)$ at the direct initial index is sent by the inverse composition comparison to its nested initial insertions: first at $(U,hu)$ for $h$, then at $(U,h^mhu)$ for $h^m$. Both sides of the displayed equality return its label $x$. The initial coprojections are isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], so this checks the entire inverse-image comparison, not just selected sections. For module pullback the corresponding calculation is $(x\otimes1)\otimes1\mapsto x\otimes1$; the tensor relations and sheafification defining [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give the same equality. The coefficient identifications agree: each is the map preserving constant sections, as specified by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]; equivalently the two adjoint maps from the constant sheaf agree on its generating constant presheaf. Thus these are the canonical composition comparisons with the coefficient maps in the statement.

proof.text:
The class of $C(T_m)$ is exactly $t_m$ under the termwise models of Step 1. Indeed, choose a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], on the ringed site $(s_{\mathrm{proet}},A_s)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], $t_{m,P}$ is the inverse of the class of the ordinary comparison $(h^{m+1})^*P\to h^*(h^m)^*P$, hence is the class of $T_{m,P}$. Every pullback here is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], so the arrows from $P$ to $K$ become isomorphisms after applying the termwise pullbacks, by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Naturality of the specified derived composition comparison and of the ordinary comparison then gives
$$t_{m,K}=Q_{m+1}(P\to K)\,t_{m,P}\,(Q_1Q_m(P\to K))^{-1},$$
and the identical conjugation formula for the class of $T_{m,K}$. They are therefore equal. This checks the normalization on arbitrary complexes, without assuming that a bounded constructible representative is K-flat. Localize the chain-map equality of Step 5 and apply evaluation, which preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. The definition of $\iota$ identifies its class with that chain map, so the resulting equality is $\iota_N^{(m+1)}=V(t_{m,N})\iota_{Q_mN}^{(1)}\iota_N^{(m)}$.

It remains to check naturality for every derived morphism, rather than only chain maps. Step 3, applied termwise, proves $V(Q_ru)\iota_N^{(r)}=\iota_{N'}^{(r)}V(u)$ for each chain map. If $w:K\to L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, both $V(w)$ and $V(Q_rw)$ are invertible by Step 1. Multiplying that equality on the left by $V(Q_rw)^{-1}$ and on the right by $V(w)^{-1}$ gives
$$V(Q_rw)^{-1}\iota_L^{(r)}=\iota_K^{(r)}V(w)^{-1}.$$
Hence naturality holds also for the formal inverse of $w$, and it is preserved by composition. The localization defining [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] constructs every derived morphism from chain maps and these formal inverses, so it holds for all derived morphisms. Finally restrict to the full subcategory $D^b_c(s,A)$: its stability under all $Q_r$ was checked in Step 1, and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] identifies $V$ there with termwise $\Gamma(s,-)$. Both the composition equality and the naturality equality are thus in the exact categories and for the exact point-fiber maps asserted in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem point_transport_composition (n : ℕ) : (∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → ∀ N : (intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) (Spec (.of D.k))).FullSubcategory, pointPowerTransportFiniteConstructible D l hl E (m + 1) n N = pointPowerTransportFiniteConstructible D l hl E m n N ≫ pointPowerTransportFiniteConstructible D l hl E 1 n ((pointPowerFinitePullback D l hl E m n).obj N) ≫ (pointFiniteFibre D l hl E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n))).map (pointPowerComposition D l hl E n m N)) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → ∀ (N N' : (intrinsicFiniteTorsionConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n)) (Spec (.of D.k))).FullSubcategory) (f : N ⟶ N'), pointPowerTransportFiniteConstructible D l hl E r n N ≫ (pointFiniteFibre D l hl E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n))).map ((pointPowerFinitePullback D l hl E r n).map f) = (pointFiniteFibre D l hl E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.zero_le n))).map f ≫ pointPowerTransportFiniteConstructible D l hl E r n N')
